kind: Sanitized bounded read-only static startup trace correlated with previously preserved crash registers

candidate_identity.identity_source: chr-7.24.4-candidate-offline-crash-2026-10-05.json; disk extraction owned by another agent, not repeated here
candidate_identity.historical_limit: Do not transfer the new candidate's register inference to the older experiment without its own register evidence. Historical sys2 byte equality to release is not a new comparison of the current candidate.

tools: Python hashlib SHA-256 over whole files
Capstone CS_ARCH_X86/CS_MODE_32 with virtual addresses mapped through ELF PT_LOAD headers
readelf -rW and -Ws for PLT relocation and symbol resolution
method.scope: Selected startup functions and executable-section scan for direct branches to the observed fault. No whole-program correctness claim or complete indirect control-flow graph.
method.command_issue: One initial Python fingerprint command had a syntax error and executed no analysis; corrected command completed. No unit or boot tests run.

branches.success_condition: If A is byte from 0x0805840f and B from 0x08053144, A*B == A*A. A==0 also passes; not an unconditional equality check.

branches.failure_edge: fallthrough to 0x0805bfd3 when je 0x0805bfdc is not taken
branches.success_condition: If A is byte from 0x0805840f and B from 0x08053144, A*B == B*B. B==0 also passes.

fault_and_known_predecessors.scan_result: Three decoded direct conditional jumps target 0x0805bfd3, plus the adjacent conditional fallthrough. No completeness claim for indirect branches or corrupted execution.
fault_and_known_predecessors.historical_correction: The older crash JSON listed two known checks, not an exhaustive predecessor set. This new trace expands that known subset without modifying historical evidence.

register_inference.source: Two records in the already-completed actual candidate overlay; not a new runtime trace
normal_path_reasoning: 0x6ed4 == 173 * 164 exactly; the first branch preserves this EAX into the faulting NULL store.
At the two buffer-product checks, normal execution leaves EBX as a zero-extended byte squared, at most 65025. Recorded EBX is much larger.
At 0x0805b67f, normal execution leaves EAX as an unsigned byte times 22. 0x6ed4 is not divisible by 22 and exceeds 255*22.
EFLAGS 0x202 has ZF clear, consistent with the first unequal comparison.
register_inference.conclusion: Among the identified normal instruction paths, both records support failure at 0x0805a9ef: the lookup returned 173 instead of expected 164. They do not support attributing the actual candidate fault to the historical pair-buffer checks.
register_inference.limits: This is register/static-code correlation, not recorded branch execution. Preceding memory corruption, unexpected control flow, or corrupted crash state are not absolutely excluded. The common EIP alone cannot distinguish the checks.

constructor.forwarded_call: 0x0003886d calls PLT 0x00023130, relocation slot 0x0007f44c resolves nv::Looper::connectLoader at 0x0003811c
constructor.arguments: 27 unsigned-word arguments forwarded in addition to this; caller includes code address/range descriptors. Their complete semantic contract is not recovered.

reply_storage.serialization: 0x0003835c..0x000384c0 adds constructor arguments to the startup message; receive-side processing follows the virtual call at 0x000384ed
reply_storage.field5: 0x0003864e/0x00038668 selects reply message field 5; 0x00038672 obtains it
reply_storage.destination: 0x0003867d computes this+0x594; 0x00038685 assigns the selected flat_message through PLT 0x00024d30
reply_storage.conditionality: Field 5 presence is checked at 0x00038651..0x0003865b; assignment is conditional. Subsequent processing can populate field 2. This is not a claim that every lookup byte was sent verbatim by loader.

lookup.table: 0x080586a7 adds 0x594; 0x080586ac selects raw field 0x688; 0x080586b3 gets its buffer
lookup.index_buffer: 0x080586c1 adds 0x594; 0x080586c6 selects raw field 2; 0x080586ca gets its buffer
lookup.expression: 0x080586d8 reads unsigned index_buffer[14]; 0x080586dc reads unsigned table[index]; 0x080586f2 returns that byte
lookup.established_relation: Reply field 5 feeds the Looper message state from which raw field 0x688 and raw field 2 supply the failing lookup.

unresolved_hypotheses.hypothesis: The loader LICENSE anchor change affects startup reply content or its client-side decoding/initialization.
unresolved_hypotheses.support: A concrete constructor/connectLoader/message-state dependency exists and the actual fault is a lookup inconsistency.
unresolved_hypotheses.missing: No anchor-to-handler dataflow or matched experiment proves that changing this anchor changes the relevant table/index. Do not label it established self-integrity, anti-tamper, or licensing behavior.

unresolved_hypotheses.hypothesis: Other changed components, package representation, or startup state affect the same message state.
unresolved_hypotheses.support: Historical repacked/signed NPK differs beyond the three decoded program byte ranges; an identical-NPK rewrite control did not isolate repacking/signing from anchor changes.
unresolved_hypotheses.missing: No demonstrated metadata/inode-to-lookup dependency; no basis to claim inode numbering causes this failure.

causal_correction: The earlier statement 'Modifying loader alters reply table ... leading directly' exceeded the evidence and is withdrawn. The startup dependency and observed inconsistency are established at the scopes above; loader-anchor causation remains a hypothesis.

next_controlled_experiment.reported_plan_not_executed_here: Another agent is preparing a pristine-vendor full-guard variant that preserves only loader's LICENSE anchor while applying the intended keyman/mode changes. No checks are disabled.
requirements: Pin input, engine, signing identity and every output hash; compare decoded content and metadata and retain differences beyond the intended loader anchor.
Use matched isolated VM configuration and fresh disposable overlays; preserve the existing baseline and capture sanitized branch/register outcomes, not just login/no-login.
If restored-loader variant changes the outcome, treat that as evidence for loader-anchor involvement under this setup, not proof of table-generation algorithm or sole root cause.
If it fails at the same check, compare table/index state under observational debugging if separately authorized; do not skip or modify the check.

Do not bypass the repository coverage guard to build a zero-replacement control. Any repack-only control needs a separately approved diagnostic method that does not masquerade as a successful guarded firmware build.
